dataset.name: Sap Velocity Data for Urban Trees in Chicago, Illinois (2024-2025)
description: This dataset contains uncorrected sap velocity measurements using the heat ratio method (HRM) collected using ICT International SFM1x sensors at five urban sites in Chicago, Illinois, as part of the DOE CROCUS project. The data includes continuous monitoring of sap velocity from various tree species, including Maples (Acer spp.): Sugar Maple (Acer saccharum), Silver Maple (Acer saccharinum), and Red Maple (Acer rubrum); Oaks (Quercus spp.): Swamp White Oak (Quercus bicolor); American Elm (Ulmus americana); Honey Locust (Gleditsia triacanthos); Cottonwood (Populus deltoides); and Tree of Heaven (Ailanthus altissima) across Chicago State University (CSU), Northeastern Illinois University (NEIU), Northwestern University (NU), University of Illinois Chicago (UIC), and West Woodlawn "Blacks in Green" (BIG). These include both street trees and those in urban park locations. Measurements were collected at 15-20 minute intervals, depending on the sensor, and transmitted via Long Range Wide Area Network (LoRaWAN) protocols. The wireless data was collected by Sage Network (https://sagecontinuum.org/) nodes. The dataset includes sensor ID, Global Positioning System (GPS) coordinates, tree species (common and scientific names), tree identification number, diameter at breast height (DBH in cm), uncorrected sap velocity measurements (cm/hr) from both inner and outer probes, and Sage Node identifiers so the data can be mapped to related variables such as air quality and wind speed that were collected on the Sage nodes. All timestamps are in local Chicago time (CDT/CST). Quality control flags are provided using a 3-bit binary system indicating physical range violations (< -10 or > 60 cm/hr), step spikes (absolute difference > 36 cm/hr), and stuck sensor conditions (> 10 consecutive identical values). These are raw data, not corrected for wood anatomy or species-specific characteristics. Data is provided in comma separated (CSV) format. This dataset is part of a larger collection of CROCUS environmental monitoring data, including linked datasets from Air Quality Transmitter (AQT) sensors, Weather Transmitter (WXT) sensors, and Multi-Function Research LoRaWAN (MFR) Nodes. DOIs for the supporting data are provided as part of this data package.

measurementTechnique:
Step 1: Sensor Installation and Data Collection
ICT International SFM1x sap flow meters were installed at breast height (1.37 m) on selected trees across five urban sites in Chicago, Illinois. These probes use the Heat Ratio Method (HRM) to estimate sap velocity at two depths in the tree. The sensors are installed parallel to each other and equidistant from a heat source in between the two probes. Sensors were installed using a drill guide to ensure parallel installations and holes were drilled using a dremel at slow speed to minimize burning of wood that affects hydraulic properties of the wood. We followed best practices for installation as described in the manufacturer’s (ICT) instructions. The sensor includes an onboard data logger that triggers a heat pulse at a user-defined interval and strength (between 20-40 joules). The system then measures the temperature ratio between upper and lower probes that is used to calculate sap velocity following established equations. Each sensor provides measurements at two sapwood depths (inner and outer probes), yielding two independent velocity measurements per sensor (uncorrected inner and uncorrected outer sap flow velocity in cm/hr). Raw data were transmitted via LoRaWAN to SAGE network nodes and collected at 15-20 minute intervals depending on sensor configuration.
Metadata recorded for each sensor includes: unique sensor ID (SX61XXXX format), GPS coordinates (latitude/longitude), tree species (common and scientific names), tree ID number, diameter at breast height (DBH in cm), site ID (CSU, NEIU, NU, UIC, BIG), and SAGE node ID.
Sensor deployment occurred in phases: CSU (July 2024), UIC (July 2024), NU (October 2024), NEIU (October 2024), and BIG (November 2024). Some sensors were relocated or replaced during the monitoring period to address installation issues or tree health concerns.

Step 2: Data Extraction and Organization
Raw sap velocity data were extracted from the SAGE data repository using the sage_data_client Python library. Data were queried by filtering for the specific SAGE node VSN, measurement names (uncorrected_inner and uncorrected_outer), and device name for each sensor. Timestamps were converted from UTC to local Chicago time (CDT/CST). For each timestamp, inner and outer sap velocity measurements were paired and recorded along with the associated metadata (coordinates, species, tree ID, DBH, node ID). No corrections were applied to the raw velocity measurements, this data represents uncorrected values.

Step 3: Quality Control Flagging
A three-category binary flagging system was implemented to identify potentially problematic data. Flags are represented as 3-bit binary strings (format: Bit 2 | Bit 1 | Bit 0), where each bit indicates a specific quality issue. Multiple flags can apply simultaneously.
Physical Range Limits (Bit 2, flag value "100"): Flags measurements outside plausible sap flow velocity range (< -10 cm/hr or > 60 cm/hr). Applied independently to both inner and outer measurements. If either measurement exceeds these bounds, the record is flagged.
Step Spike Detection (Bit 1, flag value "010"): Identifies large sudden jumps between consecutive measurements. For each sensor, measurements are sorted chronologically and the absolute difference between consecutive values is calculated for both inner and outer channels. If the absolute difference exceeds 36 cm/hr for either channel, the later measurement is flagged. To avoid false positives when sensors come back online after downtime, this check is only applied to measurements within 2 hours of each other (time gap ≤ 2 hours).
Stuck Sensor/Flat-line (Bit 0, flag value "001"): Detects sensor malfunction indicated by repeated identical values. For each sensor, sequences of consecutive identical measurements are identified separately for inner and outer channels. If more than 10 consecutive identical values are found, all measurements in that sequence are flagged. This can occur, for example, if a sensor wire was cut but the sensor continue to stream data.
Example flag values: "000" = clean data (all checks passed), "100" = physical range violation only, "010" = step spike only, "001" = stuck sensor only, "110" = physical range and step spike, "111" = all three quality issues detected. Flagged data should be carefully considered before analysis, as it is not necessarily invalid.
